title: Quantitative Researcher
tagline: Behavioral health research, measurement design, and mixed-methods analysis.
summary: Researcher with a Ph.D. in Cognitive Psychology and nine years designing, running, and analyzing behavioral health studies, including large-scale clinical trials on cognitive aging. Works across mixed methods — instrument development, survey fielding, qualitative analysis, and quantitative analysis from descriptives through structural equation modeling — and brings four years of industry data engineering in SQL and Python to data preparation and reporting. Published in peer-reviewed health and aging journals.

bullets: Design custom analyses out of exploratory investigation, tailoring method and reporting to the question each stakeholder is actually asking.
Extract and join data from large, complex sources in Microsoft SQL Server, then clean, merge, and reshape it in Python for analysis.
Built an automated reporting pipeline that calls an LLM to generate written insights alongside the quantitative results.
Build analytics reports and dashboards for internal teams and external stakeholders, and validate output from established predictive models.
Led statistical analysis for large-scale behavioral clinical trials on healthy cognitive aging, working across longitudinal datasets and multiple analysis platforms.
Designed and programmed studies end to end, preparing and submitting the IRB applications and building and fielding survey instruments in Qualtrics.
Established statistical performance norms and built regression models identifying the variables that drive cognitive outcomes.
Integrated qualitative data from surveys and interviews with quantitative measures to produce findings neither stream would support alone.
Published results in peer-reviewed journals and presented findings at national conferences.
